sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Agreement for the Reciprocal Protection and Encouragement of Investments (2007)
France-Hong Kong SAR Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (2010)
France-United States Double Taxation Convention (2009, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-44 and R.561-1 to R.561-16; Décret n°2017-1290 du 28 août 2017 (UBO declaration); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-1, L.123-5-1, R.123-130 et seq.; Ordonnance n°2020-115 du 12 février 2020 on beneficial ownership transparency
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted to designated authorities and persons demonstrating legitimate interest, per CJEU jurisprudence and AMLD5 interpretation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each shareholder, manager and beneficial owner (foreign natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / corporate existence and good standing (for foreign corporate shareholders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or business registry of shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified copy of draft articles of association (statuts) signed by all shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary (if real property contribution) or all shareholders in private deed with certified signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in France or apostille/certification if executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of source of funds for initial capital contribution
UBO declaration form (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative of the company filing at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Filed electronically via Guichet unique; no apostille for domestic form

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP screening under CMF Art. L.561-10 and R.561-11 for each shareholder, UBO, manager, and signatory; screening against UN Security Council consolidated list, EU Council Regulations (2580/2001, 881/2002), OFAC SDN list, French Ministerial lists, TRACFIN/FinCEN advisories, and negative media databases. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for high-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed foreign persons, and unusual wire transfers. Beneficial and legal title holders must be reviewed under the French anti-money laundering provisions of the Code monétaire et financier on a continuous basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités des entreprises (procedures.inpi.fr) - INPI; company name database checked via RNCS (Registre National des Sociétés) and Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be stated in French legal documentation and French is the mandatory language for all legal notices. Names using non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters in the declaration. Names in foreign languages are permissible only if written in Latin script, not contrary to French public policy, and not misleading as to the legal form or business activity. A secondary fictitious/business name is allowed but must not be identical or confusingly similar to earlier registered names or trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory name-reservation system; the availability search and clearance are preliminary. If the Guichet unique rejects the chosen name, the applicant may: (1) file an informal challenge within 30 days of rejection to the Directeur régional de l'INPI via registered letter with the rejection notice; (2) if rejected administratively, file a legal appeal before the Tribunal judiciaire (commercial chamber) or the Cour d'appel de Paris within 60 days of the administrative rejection; (3) alternatively, submit a revised company name electronically after confirming absence of conflicting names/trademarks. No extension of any reservation window is available because no reservation is recognized.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the registered office (siège social) via a third-party domiciliation provider approved under Code de commerce Article L.123-11-1. However, for a cross-dock / overseas warehouse / 3PL fulfilment business, the tax administration and customs authorities expect a separate operational physical presence in France (warehouse or logistics premises). A purely virtual office without any operational facility would create material substance risk for VAT, permanent establishment, and customs-bonded warehousing.

stage_1.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium quantified risk of 35-45% over the first 12 months; unannounced inspections may be conducted by URSSAF (social security), DGCCRF (competition and fraud), customs (for bonded/ 3PL), and local commercial registry auditors to verify registered office, stock handling, and substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code) Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq.; Décret n° 84-406 on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), filed via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) executed by all partners, the standard incorporation form (formulaire M0), and all supporting annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital for a SARL. Capital may be set as low as EUR 1; cash contributions must be fully subscribed and deposited into an escrow account with an approved French bank or notary before RCS filing, and can be withdrawn only upon issuance of the registration certificate. In-kind contributions are fully paid automatically.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the draft articles of association and share subscription of the SARL are approved, and the capital commitments are acknowledged. RESOLVED, that the registered office is located at the address set forth in the articles, and the company's domicile is adopted. RESOLVED, that the undersigned individuals are appointed as gérants (managers) with sole authority to operate the business. RESOLVED, that each gérant is empowered to open corporate bank accounts, engage employees, sign customer agreements, and complete all RCS filing, publication, and regulatory formalities. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption, the partners having voted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the articles of association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional; if local practice requires) or private contract with signatures of all partners; eventually filed with the Greffe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare statutory clauses in French, covering corporate form (SARL), company name, minimum share capital, number and rights of shares, gérant appointment, registered office address, object clause limited to ISIC 5210 cross-dock logistics and overseas e-commerce order fulfillment, and management authority. Execute the statutes in one original per partner plus an original for the registry. If a notary is engaged, have the notary retain a certified original and issue a notarial attestation.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Proof of French address or registered office entitlement (lease, utility invoice, or owner's consent)
Certified registration extracts for any corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the draft is informally queried, amend the statutory clauses as a preliminary step before formal submission; all partners must sign the amended page or execute a correcting resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French bank, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-negotiable professional account in the name of the 'société en formation' and deposit the full amount of the subscribed cash capital. Obtain the depositary's certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds) stating the total capital and the amount deposited, which must accompany the M0 filing.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association or a copy accepted by the depositary
Know-your-customer documentation for all individuals and entities
Release instructions including the future IBAN of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires supplementary compliance information, provide a source-of-funds declaration and a notarized confirmation of subscribers. The escrow amount remains in custody; a substitute depositary may be appointed without loss of the capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the incorporation legal notice in a legal announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcement venue or newspaper (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office, selected from the prefecture's official list.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a formal notice in French stating the proposed corporate name, SARL form, share capital, registered office, object, details of the gérants, and the RCS registry where registration will occur. Obtain the publisher's certificate of publication (attestation de parution), which is a mandatory attachment to the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and object clause
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal notice is challenged or returned, correct the notice and republish immediately; a revised attestation de parution must be issued before submission to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the M0 dossier with the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises, administered by the INPI and transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the online portal, select 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL)' and the activity code 5210 (warehousing and cross-dock storage). Complete the standard declarative forms, upload the statutes, capital deposit certificate, legal publication attestation, proof of registered office, identity documents, and declarations of compatibility. Pay the statutory filing fee by electronic payment. The portal issues a receipt and forwards the file to the competent Greffe for examination and entry on the RCS.
required_dossiers: M0 registration form generated by the portal
Power of attorney if filed through a representative (original or secure e-signature)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a deficiency or query (observation), correct the identified elements directly in the portal and resubmit within the prescribed delay. Additional publication is not required unless the correction materially modifies a statutory element. Any refusal may be cured by amending and resubmitting; the statutory maxima for cure are observed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the RCS registration certificate and complete post-registration obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office; INSEE issues the SIREN/SIRET numbers and APE code.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, download the official Kbis extract from the RCS portal and verify the corporate identity, SIREN, NIC, APE code, legal form, registered office, and gérant details. Ensure automatic social security and tax registration via the CFE/Guichet Unique; open the corporate bank account using the Kbis and adopt an initial internal protocol for transaction approvals.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening documents and initial resolution instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SIREN/SIRET numbers are not generated within the service window, request activation from INSEE through the Guichet Unique. Any error in the Kbis data must be corrected by filing a registry modification with the Greffe, generally within one month of discovery.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for standard ISIC 5210 cross-dock and overseas order fulfillment; however, the facility may fall under the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) regime administered by the Ministry for Ecological Transition through DREETS/DDT if storage thresholds are exceeded.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating license for cross-dock logistics in France; the RCS Kbis registration is the sole operating permit. Facilities above ICPE thresholds must hold a registration or authorization under environmental law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion (Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques) and delegated local DREETS / DDT bodies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For conventional dry cross-docking and low-fire-risk warehouses, a full environmental impact assessment is generally not required. If stored volumes of combustible goods (e.g. packaging, cardboard, wood) exceed ICPE nomenclature 1510 thresholds, an 'enregistrement' (registration) or 'autorisation' (permit) is required; otherwise the site is regarded as a routine non-ICPE logistics facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Facility wastewater must meet municipal sewer acceptance limits under local sanitation regulations, with pre-treatment for oil/grease separation where vehicle washing occurs. Domestic effluent parameters (BOD5, COD, suspended solids) must comply with national discharge standards. Packaging waste and plastics must be separately collected, temporarily stored, and transferred via licensed waste operators in accordance with the Code de l'environnement Articles L.541-2 and R.541-45. All heating and backup power installations must comply with emission standards applicable to combustion appliance exhausts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance and periodic inspection by SDIS (Service départemental d'incendie et de secours); structural load conformity certified by an approved inspection bureau (Bureau de Contrôle); electrical installation safety certification; and the mandatory workplace health and safety assessment (Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques) filed with CARSAT and the labor inspectorate (DREETS). These local clearances confirm the physical, structural, and occupational fitness of the cross-dock facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – France; business portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate registration greffe: RCS via Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE issues SIREN/SIRET and VAT identification through DGFiP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first appoint a French tax representative (if non-EU) and file the DGFiP form 'Formulaire de demande d'identification TVA' (form 1545) or register through the DGFiP Pro online service. French-established entities obtain a SIREN/SIRET via the Centre de Formalités de Entreprises (CFE) and subsequently receive a VAT intra-community (TVA) number from the Centre des impôts. For a SARL, the SIREN/SIRET is granted upon RCS registration; the VAT number is issued automatically to the registered business address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SARL (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) is subject to French corporate income tax (IS) by default. A SARL may elect for pass-through / income tax treatment (IR) under Article 239 bis AA CGI for small businesses (turnover < €10 million) and satisfying 50+ individual shareholder conditions. Additionally, an EURL (single-member SARL) may apply for quasi-partnership transparency. Hybrid mismatch elections are governed by the EU ATAD rules incorporated in French tax law (Article 212 bis CGI), applying to both inbound and outbound payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for establishment; a French SARL must register for VAT from its first taxable transaction. For small businesses, an optional exemption ('franchise en base de TVA') applies below an annual turnover of €91,900 for goods (including cross-dock warehouse resale) and €36,800 for services (including fulfillment services), but this is an option and does not apply to cross-border or intra-community acquisitions. Mandatory registration applies immediately if the entity engages in taxable activities above the de minimis handling.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates electronic invoicing for all B2B domestic transactions as of 1 September 2026 (large taxpayers) and 1 September 2027 (SMEs). E-invoicing is transmitted through a government-certified 'PDP' platform interfacing with the DGFiP; e-reporting is required for B2C and international sales via PDPs. There is no real-time digital stamping; instead, the French clearance model uses an E-invoice data warehouse (Archives). Failing to issue e-invoices through a certified PDP will result in penalties under Article 1737 CGI.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically leaving the EU are eligible for 0% VAT under Article 262 I CGI, provided the supplier obtains proof of export within 90 days. Cross-border B2B services (e.g., logistics, warehousing, cross-docking) provided to a taxable customer outside France but within the EU are zero-rated under Articles 259, 259-0, and 262-0; services related to immovable property are taxed in the country of location. A French SARL supplying 3PL services to an overseas Amazon vendor (non-taxable or localized outside France) must verify the customer's VAT number and maintain a recapitulative statement for intra-community supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EAD / DAU) with validated exit from France
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing transport outside the EU
Intra-community Sale Invoice and any supporting delivery order issued in the cross-dock warehouse
Proof of payment of freight or third-party transport document (CMR / CIM)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT statement proving payment transfer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration may reassess within a standard limitation period of three years (6-10 years for fraud). Incorrect zero-rating claims lead to VAT recovery plus interest (intérêts de retard) at 0.2% per month, a 40% ‘insuffisance de déclaration’ penalty (80% for deliberate misconduct under Article 1729 b CGI) and potential criminal fines up to €750,000 and imprisonment. Customs may also claim duty deficiencies and recover VAT under Articles 410-411 of the French Customs Code for false export declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as central bank and balance-of-payments statistics authority within the Eurosystem; foreign exchange policy is set jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) and the European Central Bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. France imposes no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Articles 63-66 TFEU and the French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF Articles L151-1 et seq.) guarantee free movement of capital, trade settlement, profit remittance, shareholder loans and capital repatriation. No FX authorisation is required. The only material remittance hurdle is the standard 25% domestic withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, commonly reduced under double tax treaties. Statistical, not restrictive, balance-of-payments declarations apply when monthly cross-border flows to a single non-resident counterparty exceed 12,500 EUR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio exist for export receipts. A French SARL may freely retain foreign-currency proceeds in multi-currency accounts or convert to EUR via the interbank market. The only compliance duties are (i) monthly Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting for cross-border receipts above 12,500 EUR per counterparty per calendar month, and (ii) customs declaration for physical cash movements equal to or above 10,000 EUR under EU Regulation 2018/1672.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) + Operational Multi-Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as ancillary payment rails: Airwallex, Wise Business and Payoneer operate under ACPR/PSD2 e-money institution passporting, providing multi-currency virtual accounts, marketplace settlement sweeps and efficient FX pricing. Feasibility rating: High for inbound collection and outbound mass payouts; Low for capital escrow, blocked accounts, tax remittance and credit facilities. The French tier-1 bank account must remain the dominant master account, with EMI funds swept daily and fully reconciled against the SARL ledger and French VAT/Intrastat obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under ACPR guidance provided the bank uses a certified video-identification process consistent with CMF Article R561-5-1. In practice, tier-1 French banks require at least one physical interview at a French branch for non-resident gérants (managers) or any UBO holding more than 25% of the SARL, unless an appropriately authorised French-resident representative with a notarised power of attorney opens the account. EU/EEA-resident managers can often onboard via enhanced video KYC with notarised identity documents, professional references and source-of-funds evidence. Non-EEA-resident managers should expect physical attendance or a biometric-enabled apostilled identity file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident 100% shareholding routed through an offshore intermediate holding company with opaque ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organogram; certified passport copies and proof of address for all natural-person UBOs; extract of the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filed with the French Commercial Court; certificates of incorporation and registers of directors of each intermediate entity; source-of-wealth memorandum and bank reference letter per UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity 3PL cross-dock flows with commingled client settlements and marketplace payouts (Amazon, Cdiscount, Fnac Darty).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed 3PL service agreements and cross-dock contracts; audited client sub-ledger demonstrating segregated accounting; marketplace settlement reports and payout statements; EORI number, customs DAE/DAO declarations and bonded warehouse receipts proving physical fulfilment; statutory auditor's opinion on transaction integrity and funds reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border receipts or disbursements touching high-risk jurisdictions, sanctions-sensitive sectors, or a volatile supplier/customer value chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EORI and customs clearance history; CMR/airway bill and bill-of-lading copies; sanctions screening output; product description and export-control classification confirming no dual-use or prohibited goods; counterparty KYC file with beneficial-owner registers; legal due-diligence memo on trade parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate lump-sum capital injection or shareholder loan relative to declared share capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised SARL incorporation deed and notarised minutes approving the capital increase; share subscription and deposit certificates; written 'avance en compte courant d'associé' agreement with interest terms; source-of-funds file for each lender (recent bank statements, tax returns, sale-and-purchase agreements); bank certificate of blocked deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-tripping: funds enter France and are repatriated to the foreign shareholder within a single settlement cycle, bypassing genuine treasury needs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade documentation chain (purchase orders, invoices, freight forwarder receipts, customs clearance); 12-month board-approved cash-flow forecast demonstrating working-capital demand; written commitment to maintain minimum operating balances in France for at least 180 days; monthly reconciliation between inflow receipts, inventory movements and outbound trade payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital must be fully subscribed and, for cash contributions, deposited in a French credit institution or with a notary before the SARL is registered with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce. The compliant wire routing is a SWIFT MT103 referencing 'Apport en capital – SARL [entity name]' with the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment ('Investissement Direct – Prise de participation dans une société résidente'). The depositary bank issues the capital-blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) delivered to the Registrar. Amounts above 12,500 EUR per non-resident counterparty per month must be included in the monthly BOP declaration, and the onboarding file must contain the incorporation deed, RBE filing receipt, notarial attestation and source-of-funds evidence for the depositing shareholder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EEA suppliers and intra-EU vendors: SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) and SEPA Direct Debit. For rest-of-world trade settlements: SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-bank wires with embedded invoice and purchase-order references and appropriate BOP declaration codes; documentary collections (CAD/DP/DA) for mid-value transactions; and SWIFT MT700/MT707 commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 for high-value CIF imports requiring transport and insurance documents. Fintech EMI rails (Airwallex, Wise, Payoneer) are permissible for marketplace seller disbursements and multi-currency mass payouts, provided daily cash sweeps to the French master account and reconciliation against VAT, Intrastat and balance-of-payments filings are maintained.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX forwards under ISDA 2002 or French FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreements, with tenors up to 24 months
Plain vanilla EUR/FX swaps (FX swaps) to manage EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CNY working-capital rollovers
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to align interest and principal flows on foreign-currency shareholder loans or local financing
European-style FX options and zero-cost EUR collars executed with ACPR-regulated investment service providers, subject to EMIR trade reporting and margining thresholds
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted Asian currencies (CNY, KRW, INR) through supervised ACPR/EU counterparties, used only for genuine exposure management of cross-border trade flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements (Dépôt des comptes annuels) filed with the RCS, comprising balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, notes and auditor's report when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of each financial year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, due by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalty up to EUR 15,000 (approx. USD 16,200) for the managing director; formal judicial notice followed by RCS administrative strike-off (radiation); risk of dissolution if non-compliance persists for two consecutive years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax return (Déclaration de résultats, liasse fiscale n°2065-SD) and final corporate income tax payment (form n°2571)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day of the fourth month following the close of the financial year; for calendar-year companies, due by 3 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% (10% if filed after 30 days), 0.20% per-month late-payment interest, automatic or discretionary reassessment of taxable profit, and administrative fines for repeated non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of company data in the National Business Register (Confirmation annuelle des données du Registre National des Entreprises – RNE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques (INSEE) through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each year within 30 days of the anniversary of the company's initial RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal RNE warning after the deadline; prolonged non-confirmation suspends official attestations and may trigger an RCS procedure for involuntary strike-off (radiation d'office)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (commissaire aux comptes) if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following at the financial year-end: balance sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees above 50. An audit also becomes mandatory if shareholders representing at least 1/10 of the capital demand it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS permitted only for consolidated accounts of listed groups, not for SARL individual accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO declaration is required. The RCS UBO register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) must be updated within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership (direct/indirect holding over 25% of capital or voting rights, or effective control). During the mandatory annual RNE data confirmation, the company must verify the consistency of all UBO and corporate data and report any discrepancy. Each quota transfer must also be recorded in the share-transfer register held at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and corporate decisions (Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)
Share-Transfer Register (Registre des mouvements de titres)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 – 16,000 per year (EUR 5,000 – 15,000) when statutory audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A qualifying small enterprise may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million, paid-in capital is fully paid and at least 75% of the capital is held by individuals or qualifying companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The principal incentive is the 15% small-enterprise rate on qualifying profit. Other incentives may include the research tax credit, innovation tax credit, regional investment incentives and temporary sector-specific regimes, subject to statutory eligibility, documentation and EU State-aid limits. No general tax holiday applies to a standard French SARL conducting logistics or fulfillment activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. Utilization is generally capped annually at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. A carryback election is generally limited to the immediately preceding fiscal year and is subject to statutory limits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through EDI-TDFC using an authorized intermediary or through the French tax administration's professional online services. The return is accompanied by the applicable 2058 and 2059 tax computation schedules and accounting annexes, including 2058-A for the tax reconciliation and 2058-B for tax loss tracking.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with corporate income tax installments generally payable quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May, subject to the current-year administrative calendar. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the final balance generally due on the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due on 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year dates, tax office and accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SARL as the French taxable entity. Foreign shareholder details belong in ownership, related-party or beneficial-owner records and do not replace the SARL's French identification data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the corporate income tax regime, applicable turnover information and whether the company is within a tax consolidation or other special regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent does not by itself make the French SARL transparent or exempt. Report the SARL's French tax regime and French accounting results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start with accounting profit or loss and record non-deductible expenses, exempt income, timing differences, taxable add-backs and allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-parent expenses unless they are genuine, documented, arm's-length charges benefiting the French entity and properly allocated under French transfer-pricing principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax losses brought forward, losses utilized, current-year losses and remaining loss balances subject to the French utilization limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not use losses of a foreign group company in the French return unless a legally applicable French tax consolidation or other statutory regime permits the utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable income after tax adjustments and loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributable to the French SARL's operations, including service, warehousing, handling and fulfillment income. Foreign-source items must be analyzed under French source and treaty rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable or exempt capital gains, provisions, depreciation adjustments and relevant tax treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French rules to assets and provisions recorded by the SARL. Treaty relief cannot convert French-company gains into exempt income without a specific legal basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate corporate income tax, credits, installments, prepayments, balance due and any refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% rate or the qualifying 15% small-enterprise rate only after confirming all statutory conditions. Claim credits only where supporting records and eligibility conditions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose shareholdings, related entities, tax consolidation information and relevant transactions where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the foreign parent, controlled affiliates, intercompany loans, management charges, royalties, guarantees and other related-party flows where the applicable French forms require them.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Validate the electronic filing, retain the electronic acknowledgment and reconcile the return with statutory accounts and general ledger balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL remains responsible for filing even where an overseas parent, service provider or foreign tax adviser prepares the data.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed corporate tax returns may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased in aggravated cases, together with late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month or the applicable statutory rate. Failure to file electronically, missing schedules, inaccurate information and payment default may generate additional fines, surcharges, loss of filing privileges and tax audit exposure. Deliberate fraud can lead to criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Forms 2571-SD, 2572-SD and related payment references for corporate income tax installments and balance payments, submitted electronically through the French professional tax portal or the company's authorized EDI intermediary.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installments plus an annual final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The final balance is generally due on the 15th day of the fourth month after fiscal year-end, subject to statutory exceptions and the current administrative calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French SIREN, tax office, relevant fiscal year and payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's tax account and SIREN, not the foreign parent's tax identifier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the required installment or final balance based on the French taxable liability and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the amount to the filed 2065 return, tax computation schedules and bank payment evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit payment through the permitted electronic payment channel and retain the confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payer's bank mandate and payment account identify the French entity and allow timely settlement in euros.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may trigger a 5% payment surcharge in addition to late-payment interest, subject to statutory exceptions and taxpayer conduct. Repeated payment failures may result in collection measures, liens, account attachment and director-level enforcement in cases involving fraudulent or deliberate conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident. A lower treaty rate or an exemption may apply. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may be available for a qualifying corporate parent, generally requiring a qualifying ownership interest, minimum holding period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions. French domestic anti-abuse rules and beneficial-ownership requirements apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and complete the applicable French forms, commonly Form 5000-FR and, for dividends, Form 5001-FR. Submit the documentation through the French payer or withholding agent where relief at source is permitted. If relief at source is unavailable or rejected, withhold at the domestic rate and request a refund from the French tax administration using the applicable treaty forms. Maintain evidence of beneficial ownership, ownership percentage, holding period, substance, anti-abuse analysis, payment date and tax residence for the statutory retention period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to a domestic withholding rate of 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and special rules for non-cooperative jurisdictions. Interest paid by a French company is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply, including payments to certain non-cooperative jurisdictions, anti-abuse situations and specific financial instruments. Treaty rates vary by recipient country and payment category. EU interest-and-royalty relief may apply where the statutory ownership, subject-to-tax, holding-period and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The principal threshold for mandatory full French transfer-pricing documentation is generally EUR 400,000,000 of annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets, or membership in or control by an enterprise or group meeting the statutory threshold. A French entity below that threshold may still need to demonstrate arm's-length pricing and may be subject to the simplified documentation regime and annual transfer-pricing declaration where the applicable EUR 50,000,000 threshold or other statutory conditions are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single standalone economic substance regulation equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance is nevertheless material under French transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-abuse rule, principal-purpose and treaty anti-abuse standards, beneficial-ownership analysis, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules and interest limitation provisions. The SARL should maintain French operational substance proportionate to its activities, including premises or operational capacity, personnel or outsourced-function governance, decision-making, inventory and risk controls, contracts, accounting records, customs evidence and commercial rationale.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing French turnover, fabricating expenses, understating taxable profit, falsifying invoices, manipulating inventory or claiming knowingly ineligible deductions or tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest and penalties that may reach 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct, together with criminal tax-fraud penalties generally including up to five years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 500,000. Aggravated fraud may carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 3,000,000, with higher penalties potentially linked to the proceeds or organized conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability, personal civil liability in cases of fraudulent or repeated tax misconduct under French tax-enforcement rules, director disqualification, professional prohibitions and asset-enforcement measures. Travel restrictions or imprisonment require judicial or criminal measures and are not automatic consequences of an ordinary tax adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing and fictitious intercompany charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the SARL for services not rendered, routing profits through sham management fees, using fabricated customs or warehouse documentation, or recording non-arm's-length related-party expenses without benefit or evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions, withholding-tax reassessment, transfer-pricing adjustment, penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80% depending on intent and conduct, late-payment interest and possible criminal prosecution for forgery, fraud or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be prosecuted where they authorized or knowingly participated in the conduct. Corporate separateness does not protect intentional personal wrongdoing or statutory management liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting French fulfillment profits to an overseas affiliate, failing to price warehousing and logistics functions at arm's length, omitting related-party transactions, or failing to provide required master-file, local-file or annual declaration documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment based on the arm's-length principle, late-payment interest, penalties for inadequate or missing documentation and a specific documentation penalty that may be significant and is generally linked to the greater of statutory fixed amounts or a percentage of the adjusted profit, subject to statutory caps.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for deliberate concealment, obstruction, fraudulent accounting or knowingly approving materially false documentation. Ordinary documentation failure normally creates corporate tax liability rather than automatic imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared permanent establishment or concealed French activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL, foreign warehouse, agents or related entities to conceal a French fixed place of business, dependent-agent activity, staff function or inventory operation that creates additional French taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate income tax, VAT, payroll and other tax assessments, interest, penalties, possible withholding-tax liability and criminal consequences where concealment is deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for fraudulent management, obstruction or tax evasion if they intentionally structured or operated the activity to conceal French taxable presence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying goods, undervaluing imports, using incorrect customs origin, omitting import VAT, misusing EORI or customs authorizations, or issuing invoices inconsistent with actual cross-border movements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, interest, administrative fines, seizure or forfeiture of goods, suspension or withdrawal of customs authorizations and criminal penalties for serious customs fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally prosecuted for intentional customs fraud, forged documents or organized evasion. Civil recovery may extend to persons who personally guaranteed or enabled the unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting or moving proceeds of crime, disguising the beneficial owner, processing suspicious third-party payments, structuring transactions to avoid controls or knowingly assisting illicit fund flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French money-laundering offenses may carry imprisonment and substantial criminal fines, with aggravated sanctions for habitual, organized or professional conduct. Assets and proceeds may be seized or confiscated. AML reporting and cooperation failures may also trigger supervisory sanctions where the entity is within an applicable regulated perimeter.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may be personally prosecuted where they knowingly participate, facilitate or conceal laundering. Imprisonment, confiscation and judicial restrictions are possible following criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial-owner concealment and sham residence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SARL as a nominal vehicle with no credible operational function, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, using nominee directors or falsely claiming treaty residence or operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of treaty benefits, denial of deductions, tax reassessment, anti-abuse penalties, beneficial-owner and registry sanctions, possible accounting or fraud offenses and confiscation where criminal conduct is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil damages, management bans, criminal prosecution and personal liability for fraudulent declarations or participation in concealment. Travel bans or imprisonment are possible only where ordered under applicable judicial or criminal procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain accounting records and obstruction of tax audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying or withholding ledgers, refusing electronic accounting-file production, backdating contracts, obstructing investigators or providing materially incomplete records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessment by estimation, increased penalties, rejection of accounting records, procedural fines and possible criminal liability for obstruction, forgery or fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and de facto manager may be personally prosecuted for deliberate obstruction or falsification. A court may impose management prohibitions, civil restitution and criminal sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend distribution or unlawful profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, bypassing statutory accounts, disguising dividends as loans or service fees, or remitting funds without applying required withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unlawful distributions, withholding-tax assessments, interest, penalties, possible director liability and criminal consequences for misuse of corporate assets or false accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be required to restore unlawfully distributed amounts and may be liable for abuse of corporate assets, breach of fiduciary duties, fraudulent accounting or tax evasion.
